rationale:
Evidence: every raced design (iterations 0, 1 and 3) left the track in all 60 trials. Progress on the s-bend is 0.040 in every race whatever kp, kd, ki, sensor size or base_speed (1.0 to 1.7) was used, and max_error sits at the 0.06 m off-track limit. A failure point that does not move with gains or speed points to a fixed early event, not a slow drift. Iteration 2's wide array, which was never raced, is the only untested change that targets the visibility problem, so it is the one I keep.

What I accept from the round-1 critique: (1) The draft changed several things at once, so I keep the wide-array geometry and change only the controller terms that the critique's arithmetic flags. (2) kd 0.8 is rejected. It doubles the derivative with no signal-rate estimate, and it would amplify the about 2 percent noise. I use kd 0.4, which was the value in the untested iteration-2 design. (3) The gain-matching point is accepted. The wide array has about 13 signal units per metre against about 25 for iteration 1. Keeping steering authority of about 75 units per metre (kp times slope) needs kp of about 5.5, not 4.5. (4) The visibility point is accepted and stated: outer sensors see tape only beyond about 0.054 m offset, so the gain varies with offset. This is a limit of the layout, not something I can fix within the range.

What I changed: base_speed 0.9 to 1.0, so the speed is no longer below the 1.0 already raced and the time term is not dropped entirely. kp 4.5 to 5.5 for matched authority, kd 0.8 to 0.4, ki kept at 0, line_loss last_direction. Mass, wheel track and radius, body and sensor y = 0.06 are unchanged.

Rejected: lowering speed further as the main test. Completion needs about 1.5 m/s, so a 0.9 run cannot finish. The useful question now is whether the robot stays on the line at all.

Predictions (guesses, not expectations): max_error below 0.06 and progress above 0.04 on the s-bend. Finishing within 3 s is unlikely at this speed. Decision rule for the next revision: if max_error is below 0.05 with line_loss_events 0 on the s-bend, raise base_speed in steps of 0.2 toward 1.5. If progress is still 0.040 on the s-bend, the cause is a start or entry transient, and the next test should change the line-loss rule or the start, not the gains.
